registeredBy: Sam (owner); no run made before this file was committed
hypothesis: Once the cycle clock reads hiking (a hike after a hold or a cut), another hike follows within 6 months more often than a hike follows any month; once it reads cutting, another cut follows within 6 months more often than a cut follows any month.
knownLimits: The idea was suggested by the leading-indicator test (cli_turn_policy v1), which failed because banks kept moving the same way after a turn. This is a new rule written after seeing that, not a re-test of it.
Hiking or cutting uses the app's own clock (src/utils/cycleClock.ts): the latest move in the past 6 months sets the state, and 6 months without a move is on hold.
Policy rates only (BIS monthly, end of month); a hike and a cut in the same month net out. Every BIS area is pooled, pegged currencies included.
Rate cycles are well known to come in runs, so a pass says the clock reads that, not that it beats a forecaster.
